subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should durable browser-tab tracking deliberately stop retrying and discard an unreachable row after 24 hours, accepting that a same-instance browser returning later will no longer receive automatic cleanup?
rationale: The code can safely implement either retry policy, but selecting the retention window changes an existing durable-cleanup expectation and cannot be resolved from tests alone.

options.title: Accept bounded retirement
options.body: Keep the fixed 24-hour policy after live-browser proof shows retirement restores new tab tracking without affecting transient outages.

options.title: Retain indefinite retry
options.body: Preserve current retry semantics and pursue a different cap-recovery design that does not discard long-unreachable ownership records.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Set a different documented retention policy if maintainers want bounded state but judge 24 hours too aggressive for expected browser downtime.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded retirement
recommendation.body: Keep the fixed 24-hour policy after live-browser proof shows retirement restores new tab tracking without affecting transient outages.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged durable-registry implementation defines the ownership and retry semantics affected by this policy choice.
